approach: Add a pure check `staleness(records, item) -> Option<String>` to crates/athena-core/src/work_decisions.rs and call it in `Athena::approve_work` right after `find_open` (line 329) and before `approve_request` (330) and `self.ask` (331). A proposal is stale when (a) a job cited in its source or evidence has a closing outcome (`later_outcome` else `outcome`, as `JobRecords::state` does) whose reason, after stripping `closed: `, starts with `Done`, recorded after the item's `at`; or (b) its source or evidence is an `audience-ratings` record path whose rating has a newer rating (later `(at, id)`) of the same target. When stale, `approve_work` returns an error that says the proposal is stale, names every closing job id and the newest newer rating id, says nothing was queued, and asks for a fresh approval. Nothing is written, so no job and no decision record exist and the proposal stays open. `approve_in_limit` (line 358-370) and the drain's `approve` both reach `approve_work`, so they are covered. drain.rs gets a doc comment only. Two in-crate tests drive `approve_work` on a seeded repo, one drives `approve_in_limit`, and a unit test covers the pure function. CHANGELOG.md and roles-and-ladder.md record the rule. Criterion 5 is shown by running the three Athena checks, with the demonstration now stating its seam and what fails without the behavior.

decisions.choice: Put the check in `approve_work` after `find_open`, before `approve_request` and `self.ask`.
decisions.reason: `approve_in_limit` (work_decisions.rs:358-370), the drain's `approve` (drain.rs:4283) and `athena approve-work` (main.rs:1046) all go through `approve_work`, so one check covers every path. It runs before building the request or asking the reader. This is the root-cause place.

rejected.option: Check in `approve_in_limit` or in the drain only
rejected.why: `athena approve-work` by hand would still queue a stale proposal.
`approve_request` is a text builder used by tests in refusal_corpus.rs (line 810, with `Records::default()`); mixing a refusal into it would change those callers.

decisions.choice: Mark stale by refusing with an error. The proposal stays open; no new record or state is written.
decisions.reason: The brief puts a new work-decision schema or stale state out of scope. The drain already keeps an erroring proposal open and prints the error (drain.rs:2059-2066), so the user sees the ids. reject-work or a re-raised proposal are the existing ways forward.

rejected.option: Append a work-decision record with a Stale state
rejected.why: Out of scope; needs a new schema and AnyRecord handling.

decisions.choice: A cited job counts as closed as done when its latest outcome reason, after stripping `closed: `, starts with `Done`, and the outcome's `at` is later than the work item's `at`.
decisions.reason: Matches the reading's definition (`close` writes `closed: {why}`, manage.rs:163; `closed_by_person` strips the same prefix, hestia.rs:352). The later-than-item time keeps a proposal that cites an old finished job only as evidence from being refused for good.

rejected.option: Treat any cited closed or landed job as stale
rejected.why: Many proposals cite landed or closed jobs as evidence of a past failure; valid proposals would be refused.

rejected.option: Ignore the time and refuse any cited Done job
rejected.why: A re-raised proposal would cite the same job and be refused forever.

decisions.choice: A rating is cited when the source or an evidence path starts with `records/audience-ratings/`; its id is the file stem. Newer means another rating with the same target and a greater `(at, id)`.
decisions.reason: `audience::work_item` (audience.rs:98-115) sets source and evidence to the rating's canonical path. `Records.audience_ratings` is sorted by `(at, id)` (store.rs:465-467). The request says 'same target', so audience name is not compared.

rejected.option: Compare with `audience::latest` (the last rating of any target)
rejected.why: A rating of a different page would wrongly make a proposal stale.

decisions.choice: No refusal_corpus case is added; `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` is run as a regression.
decisions.reason: The inputs are records (references, outcomes, ratings), not request text; `approve_request` is unchanged. Cases calling it (refusal_corpus.rs:810, `approve_request_has_the_generators_shapes` at :842) are unaffected.

rejected.option: Add corpus cases for the staleness inputs
rejected.why: The corpus replays reading checks over request text; staleness inputs never reach it.

decisions.choice: Criterion 5 is demonstrated by the full check commands plus the named tests that fail if the check is missing or too broad, not by a bare 'passes' claim.
decisions.reason: A pass of fmt, clippy and test shows the behavior only through the tests it runs: the new refusal tests fail without the check, and the existing approve_work callers fail if the check over-refuses.

rejected.option: Treat criterion 5 as a pure build gate with no seam
rejected.why: The reviewer requires a seam and a failure condition for every behavior criterion.

Comment-only: the doc comment on `approve_all` says a proposal refused as stale stays open and its reason is in the note. No behavior change.

steps: Read work_decisions.rs tests and `test_support::make_athena` for the fixture shape; check `RecordId`/`JobId` ordering and `Outcome` fields (athena-data records.rs).

In work_decisions.rs add `pub fn staleness(records: &Records, item: &WorkItem) -> Option<String>`. For each reference in source plus evidence: a `RefKind::Job` whose `records.jobs` entry has `later_outcome.as_ref().or(outcome.as_ref())` with reason (after `strip_prefix("closed: ")`) starting `Done` and `at > item.at` is a closing job. A `RefKind::Path` starting with `records/audience-ratings/` gives an id (file stem); find the rating in `records.audience_ratings`; collect ratings with the same target and greater `(at, id)`, keep the newest. Return None when neither is found. Otherwise return a message that says: work item {id} is stale, lists 'job {J} was closed as done: {reason}' and 'rating {R2} of {target} is newer than the cited rating {R1}', then says it was not queued and a fresh approval is needed (reject it with `athena reject-work {id} --why ...` and approve a proposal raised from the current records).

In `approve_work`, right after `let item = find_open(&known, id)?.clone();` (line 329), add `if let Some(why) = staleness(&known, &item) { bail!("{why}"); }` so it runs before `approve_request` and `self.ask`. Update the module doc comment. Do not touch `approve_request`, `approve_in_limit` or `find_open`.

Add a test helper that commits records into the `repo_with` repo (write `NewFile::record(&record)` bytes, `git add -A`, commit, as the existing test does near lines 542-551). Add tests: `approve_work_refuses_a_proposal_whose_cited_job_was_closed_as_done` (with a control close reason that is approved), `approve_work_refuses_a_proposal_whose_source_rating_has_a_newer_one` (with a fresh and an other-target case that are approved), `approve_in_limit_refuses_a_stale_proposal` (steward role via `athena_data::roles::steward(at())`), and the pure `staleness_names_the_closing_job_and_the_newer_rating`. Assert on no new job in `Records::load(...).jobs`, empty `work_decisions`, unchanged head, and the message text (job id, rating id, 'stale', 'fresh approval').
In drain.rs update only the doc comment on `approve_all` (around line 2026); confirm no code line changed.

Add the CHANGELOG.md entry under Unreleased > Added (format of existing entries: root cause, jobs 20261027-074457-bx8e and 20261018-000747-w4v7 as the cause, the rule, tests, 'this check refuses more approvals'). Add the sentence to roles-and-ladder.md.

Run `cargo fmt --all`, then `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked`, and `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus`. Run `git diff --stat` to confirm no change to model.json, claims.json or site.rs.

risks.risk: The check refuses a valid proposal (a false positive); the only ways forward are reject-work or a re-raised proposal.
risks.mitigation: Limit rule (a) to outcomes whose reason starts with `Done` after stripping `closed: ` and whose `at` is later than the item's `at`; rule (b) to audience-ratings paths of the same target. Tests cover the negative cases.

risks.risk: A refused proposal looks stuck to the user.
risks.mitigation: The error names the ids and says how to proceed (reject-work, then a fresh proposal from current records). The proposal stays open and the drain prints the reason.

risks.risk: The test fixture is invalid, so the refusal passes for another reason.
risks.mitigation: Test records are built through the real record types and `canonical_path()`, with outcome totals `Some(...)` as validation requires (records.rs:1215), and a control case approves a non-Done close.

risks.risk: The cited rating path form drifts from what the parser expects.
risks.mitigation: The rating test builds the item with `audience::work_item` so the cited path is the production form. A path that does not parse as a known rating is ignored (not stale), never an error.

risks.risk: A job blocked and then closed Done later is missed if only `outcome` is read.
risks.mitigation: Read the job through `later_outcome` first then `outcome`, as `JobRecords::state` does (store.rs:116-126).

demonstrations.method: Unit test `approve_work_refuses_a_proposal_whose_cited_job_was_closed_as_done` in work_decisions.rs. It builds a repo with `repo_with`, commits a work item (kind proposal, role steward, `at` 2026-10-15) whose evidence is `Reference::job(J)`, plus J's Request and an Outcome (reason `closed: Done: the items landed in 9884df5`, `at` 2026-10-16, totals `Some(crate::scoring::totals(&[], None))`). It calls `athena.approve_work(id, &Quiet)`, asserts Err, reloads `Records` and asserts no new job, empty `work_decisions`, and unchanged git head. A control in the same test uses a second repo whose J is closed `closed: dropped as a duplicate` and asserts `approve_work` succeeds.
demonstrations.observes: The Done-closed case returns an error with no new job and no decision record; the control case is approved, so the refusal comes from the check and not from the fixture.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the check, `approve_work` reads the request, asks the reader and commits an approval, so the Err assertion, the no-new-job assertion and the no-decision assertion all fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point: `Athena::approve_work` (work_decisions.rs:326), guarded by `find_open`. Fixture: `repo_with` (exists, work_decisions.rs:480) with the scripted fake reader from `test_support::make_athena` (exists), records committed as the existing test near line 534 does. A small helper that commits the extra records is added in step 4. The refusal logic is not in any double.

demonstrations.method: Unit test `approve_work_refuses_a_proposal_whose_source_rating_has_a_newer_one` in work_decisions.rs. It commits two `AudienceRating` records for the same target (older R1 at 2026-10-10, newer R2 at 2026-10-12) and a proposal built with `audience::work_item` citing R1's canonical path; `approve_work` returns Err with no job and no decision. A second proposal citing R2 (nothing newer) and a third citing a rating of another target are still approved and a decision record names each. `approve_in_limit_refuses_a_stale_proposal` records the steward role (`athena_data::roles::steward`) and asserts `approve_in_limit` refuses a stale item.
demonstrations.observes: The stale-rating proposal is refused and queues nothing; proposals citing the newest rating of their target, or a rating of another target, are approved with a job and a decision.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the rating check, the stale proposal is approved and the Err and no-decision assertions fail; a check comparing across targets would fail the unrelated-proposal-approved assertion.
